body:
I suggest two alternative takes from Calinou's.
```suggestion
			Adds the specified prefix string before the numerical value of the [SpinBox]. This is ignored if [member format] is not empty.
```
or (no negative, I prefer it)
```suggestion
			Adds the specified prefix string before the numerical value of the [SpinBox]. This is used only if [member format] is empty.
```

Also apply to `prefix`.

I don't remember the syntax as of writing this but, in order to better hint at this feature, I would heavily recommend having some sort of placeholder like `%f` as a... placeholder for the line edit.

The feature itself is a bit "unfriendly" to non-programmers. I was considering other options, like having the property default to `%s`, but at least a placeholder would be better than nothing.

Doesn't placeholder suggest it's a default value?
(That's how AcceptDialog uses it for ok button text.)

You can hover the property and see multiple examples, so it should be fine.

> Doesn't placeholder suggest it's a default value?

Well, yesn't because, you know as well as me, the editor also uses it to provide small instructions. But if we want to strictly adhere to "a default value", then it would make some sense to use `%s` as a placeholder, wouldn't it?
I think this should be reduced to something smaller, like "\<Invalid\>", since the vast majority of `SpinBox`es wouldn't be wide enough to show even half of this text.
But simple `<Invalid>` does not imply format error, so it may be unclear.
And this is not clear either, which is what most people will see: The node warning already does a better job informing what's happening.
